assessment.subject: FlowMimic mask-free video/image editing-and-generation model with pixel-pair warped flow field
assessment.object: existing curated video-editing data pipelines (mask annotation, I2V+ControlNet synthesis, VLM filtering)
assessment.claim_summary: FlowMimic generates video-editing training data in real time from image-editing samples via a pixel-pair warped flow field, letting a single model learn video editing without masks.

assessment.subject: learned soft prefixes and their effect on syllogistic reasoning in fixed LLMs
assessment.object: paired/matched random-prefix controls; Qwen3.6 MoE, Qwen3-8B, Gemma 4 31B
assessment.claim_summary: Learned soft prefixes reliably override LLMs' correct syllogistic judgments (flip 54-90% vs <1% for random controls), acting mainly through a broad answer-meaning preference rather than symbol forcing.
assessment.magnitude: flip 72-90% (Qwen), 54-56% (Gemma) vs <1% random; beat controls by 37-99 pp

assessment.subject: domain-generalized pixel-level image tampering detection (balanced minibatch sampling + late injection)
assessment.object: prior SOTA PIXAR; OOD VLM generators GPT-Images-2.0, Gemini-3.1, FLUX.2, Seedream 4.5
assessment.claim_summary: A domain-generalized training framework outperforms prior SOTA PIXAR by ~26% relative gIoU/cIoU on out-of-distribution VLM-generated image tampering localization.

assessment.subject: effect of linguistic framing of user belief expressions on LLM context vs prior-knowledge following
assessment.object: 16 LLMs (Llama3, Qwen3, Gemma3; 1B-30B; base vs instruct); 17 EoB types
assessment.claim_summary: Linguistic framing of user belief expressions systematically shifts whether LLMs follow context vs prior knowledge; larger/instruct models are less context-following, and some EoB types are significantly more persuasive.

assessment.subject: autonomous-discovery harnesses (OpenEvolve, TTT-Discover) decomposed into components
assessment.object: 30 budget-matched harnesses across 12 model-problem pairs; baseline null distributions
assessment.claim_summary: Across 30 budget-matched harnesses and 12 model-problem pairs (3.1M rollouts), no fixed discovery harness is universally superior; harness choice is a problem-specific hyperparameter, and online adaptive allocation beats fixed choices.

assessment.subject: Patch Policy: transformer robot policy consuming dense pretrained ViT patch tokens via block-causal attention
assessment.object: global-pooled-representation policies; fine-tuned OpenVLA-OFT; 4 simulated + 3 real-world suites
assessment.claim_summary: Patch Policy consumes dense pretrained ViT patch tokens, achieving ~40% relative improvement over global-pooled policies and beating OpenVLA-OFT by 18% with ~0.7% of the parameters.
assessment.magnitude: 40% rel. improvement; +18% vs OpenVLA-OFT at 0.7% params

assessment.subject: Text-Prompted Image Perceptual Similarity (TPIPS) metric + multi-aspect human similarity-judgment dataset
assessment.object: frontier VLMs; human annotator consensus; single-scalar perceptual metrics
assessment.claim_summary: A new dataset of multi-aspect human image-similarity judgments reveals a VLM-human gap; a fine-tuned VLM (TPIPS) conditions similarity on text prompts, aligning better with human perception and generalizing out of distribution.

assessment.subject: synthetic control estimator for compositional (share) outcomes via Aitchison-geometry log-odds barycenters
assessment.object: Pennsylvania electricity generation mix under the Alternative Energy Portfolio Standard vs synthetic counterfactual
assessment.claim_summary: A synthetic control estimator for compositional outcomes (Aitchison-metric Frechet barycenter of donor log-odds); applied to Pennsylvania, natural gas exceeds its counterfactual by ~60 percentage points by 2022 while renewables lose ground.
assessment.magnitude: natural gas ~60 pp above counterfactual by 2022

assessment.subject: order-theoretic transformations for lossless dimensionality reduction of equilibrium systems
assessment.object: high-dimensional equilibrium systems (economics/finance; a real-option application)
assessment.claim_summary: Order-theoretic structure yields transformations that exactly reduce high-dimensional equilibrium systems to low-dimensional ones without information loss; a real-option application shows up to 70,000x speed gains.

assessment.subject: bootstrap-based diagnostic for identifiability (multiple Gaussian shocks) in non-Gaussian SVARs
assessment.object: standard normality pre-tests on reduced-form innovations; Monte Carlo with NIG shocks
assessment.claim_summary: A bootstrap-based diagnostic detects failure of non-Gaussian SVAR identification where normality pre-tests fail; Monte Carlo shows near-exact nominal size, power rising with sample size, and no pre-testing bias.

assessment.subject: convergence-rate theory for econometric models using pre-trained deep-learning embeddings as covariates
assessment.object: double machine learning applications (partially linear regression, demand elasticity, imputation, ATE)
assessment.claim_summary: Provides sufficient conditions under which off-the-shelf pre-trained embeddings can be used reliably and derives the convergence rate of ML models with pre-trained embeddings, illustrated via double machine learning.

assessment.subject: Intra-Fold Sample-Splitting nonparametric test for the variance of the CATE (heterogeneous treatment effects)
assessment.object: existing nonparametric heterogeneity tests; NSW job-training program data
assessment.claim_summary: A novel Intra-Fold Sample-Splitting test for CATE-variance restores consistency, asymptotic normality and Type I error control; Monte Carlo shows superior size and high power, and it detects heterogeneity in NSW data that standard tests miss.

assessment.subject: partialled-out IV estimand with a machine-learned first stage; heterogeneity-robust orthogonal score
assessment.object: naive debiased moment / learner-dependent IV targets
assessment.claim_summary: The machine-learned-instrument IV estimand is a (convex, under covariance-monotonicity) signal-weighted average of heterogeneous effects; a proposed orthogonal score restores sqrt(N) inference on a learner-invariant target at no efficiency cost.

assessment.subject: effect of social integration on immigrants' housing behaviours (commute distance, rent, resale price premium)
assessment.object: native/local households; Singapore public rental vs resale housing markets (quasi-natural experiment)
assessment.claim_summary: Using a Singapore public-housing quasi-experiment and a 1,128-household survey, longer-residing immigrant renters live up to 3.04% farther from work and pay up to 0.67% lower rent per year (stronger for minorities), while naturalised citizens face no resale price premium vs natives.
assessment.magnitude: renters up to 3.04% farther, up to 0.67% lower rent/yr; no resale premium

assessment.subject: digital-twin / agent-based simulation method for evaluating local collective electricity tariffs
assessment.object: Danish Local Collective Tariff across residential energy-community configs (PV, battery, EV)
assessment.claim_summary: A digital-twin simulation integrating agent-based household modeling and tariff logic evaluates the Danish Local Collective Tariff; aggregating heterogeneous demand reduces peak coincidence and yields community-level cost reductions, sensitive to consumption-generation timing.

assessment.subject: spatial analytics framework for evaluating Ageing-in-Place practices; cross-city AIP model comparison
assessment.object: AIP models of US (San Francisco), Japan (Tokyo), Singapore
assessment.claim_summary: A cost-benefit comparison finds Singapore's Ageing-in-Place model has comparative advantage (low cost, high accessibility); a proposed spatial analytics framework quantifies alignment between ageing facilities and the ageing population.

assessment.subject: gate-and-menu economic model of collective tourism brand value with Aumann-Shapley value allocation
assessment.object: destination assets/custodians; 166 economies (measured from guide text); World Heritage List; French wine regions
assessment.claim_summary: Modeling a destination as a weaker-link 'gate' times a love-of-variety 'menu', the theory shows decentralized custodians weakly under-maintain gate quality; constructs are measured from guide text across 166 economies with a partial World Heritage external check.

assessment.subject: effect of random group/classroom assignment on student social-network formation via triadic closure
assessment.object: randomly assigned classrooms vs smaller social groups; first-year university students
assessment.claim_summary: Randomly assigning first-year students to classrooms/social groups, a subgraph-generated network model shows group assignment shapes network formation almost entirely by inducing additional triadic closure; ignoring closure gives misleading predictions.

assessment.subject: periodic directed landscape (conjectured scaling limit for periodic KPZ-universality models)
assessment.object: periodic exponential last passage percolation; periodic KPZ fixed point; periodic ASEPs
assessment.claim_summary: Constructs the periodic directed landscape as the scaling limit of periodic KPZ-class models, proves convergence of periodic LPP and ASEPs to it, and confirms Baik-Liao-Liu conjectures on the periodic KPZ fixed point's local structure.

assessment.subject: sensitivity/linear-response of entropy-regularized exploratory equilibria in time-inconsistent stochastic control
assessment.object: low-temperature Gibbs responses; positive feedback cycles vs causal paths
assessment.claim_summary: Proves the derivative of an exploratory equilibrium is governed by a backward Volterra-parabolic resolvent; positive feedback cycles yield exponential error amplification (vs polynomial for causal paths), with characterized discretization consistency and a Lambert-W transition.

assessment.subject: adaptive Digital Twin framework (Fisher-score drift detector + LoRA continual learning + Mann-Whitney U validation)
assessment.object: stochastic linear system; directed energy deposition additive-manufacturing process (case studies)
assessment.claim_summary: An adaptive Digital Twin framework detects concept drift via Fisher-score vectors, fine-tunes <1% of parameters via LoRA, and certifies improvement with a Mann-Whitney U test; on case studies it detects shifts with short delays and restores accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

assessment.subject: convergence rate of stochastic multi-gradient descent (SMG) for smooth nonconvex multi-objective optimization
assessment.object: prior O~(T^-1/4) bound of Chen et al. (2024) under the same setting
assessment.claim_summary: Proves an improved O~(T^-1) convergence rate (squared Pareto-stationarity) for stochastic multi-gradient descent with constant stepsize and linearly growing mini-batches, improving Chen et al. (2024)'s O~(T^-1/4), by exploiting Lipschitz continuity of the PS measure.
